author: Monthly Review Press
title: LIVE Oct 30, in DC! See Aymeric Monville, Jennifer Ponce de León and Gabriel Rockhill, speaking on “Requiem for French Theory”
content:
NYC, on October 29th, at CUNY (25 Broadway) * DC, on October 30th at Busboys and Poets (235 Carol St NW) * (And a couple of days ago in Philly’s Free Library)


APPEARANCES


Coming from Left Field

 (Episode 152)


In this episode of Coming From Left Field, philosopher and cultural critic Gabriel Rockhill joins

Greg Godels & Pat Cummings

 to explore the Ford Foundation, the 1966 Johns Hopkins conference often cited as a launching point for French Theory in the United States, Cold War cultural politics, and the wider political economy of academic knowledge production. Rockhill argues for rebuilding a class-centered, internationalist Marxism and joins a thoughtful exchange on China, Vietnam, socialism, imperialism, inequality, and the challenges of assessing existing socialist projects without demonization or uncritical celebration….


Marx Memorial Library

in London hosted a dual book launch for

Requiem for French Theory

 and

Who Paid the Pipers of Western Marxism?

with Gabriel Rockhill, Aymeric Monville, and Jennifer Ponce de León, who engaged in a discussion regarding the effects of imperialism on the production and dissemination of knowledge.

Watch here

or below


Far from simply engaging in a critique of the faux radicalism of the prominent discourses within the imperial theory industry, the discussion was grounded in a reasoned defense of the vibrant international tradition of anti-imperialist Marxism. Topics included the imperial promotion of Western Marxism and postmodern French Theory, the international war of ideas, the failed efforts to discredit anti-imperialist Marxism, culturalism and identity politics vs. a materialist analysis of the colonial question, fascism past and present, the dialectics of actually existing socialism, and the current state of global class struggle in theory and practice.


REVIEWS


Marxism-Leninism Today,

 by

Greg Godels

:


“During the 1960s and 1970s, it was an oft-repeated quip that the European left was long on theory and short on practice, while the North American left was strong on action, but allergic to theory. In West Germany, Italy, and France, young leftists would often passionately debate theoretical questions deep into the night, while seldom coming to a common commitment to action the next day. Their youthful U.S. counterparts—revived after the retreat from High McCarthyism–counted on spontaneous action and a firm commitment to common, inherited political values rather than the ideas buried in deep theoretical tracts. But those observations were far from completely true. The often student-driven U.S. New Left developed a thirst for a broader, deeper explanation of the injustices that they were rejecting. Many of those committed to action turned to left classics–quite often a reconsidered Marx–and others favored a wave of West European radical-oriented thinkers….”

Read more…


ZZ’s Blog

, as reviewed by Zigedy:


“During the 1960s and 1970s, it was an oft-repeated quip that the European left was long on theory and short on practice, while the North American left was strong on action, but allergic to theory. In West Germany, Italy, and France, young leftists would often passionately debate theoretical questions deep into the night, while seldom coming to a common commitment to action the next day. Their youthful US counterparts–revived after the retreat from High McCarthyism– counted on spontaneous action and a firm commitment to common, inherited political values rather than the ideas buried in deep theoretical tracts. But those observations were far from completely true. The often student-driven US New Left developed a thirst for a broader, deeper explanation of the injustices that they were rejecting. Many of those committed to action turned to left classics– quite often a reconsidered Marx– and others favored a wave of West European radical-oriented thinkers. It is the rise and importation to the US of one particularly influential “brand” of European theory to which Aymeric Monville and Gabriel Rockhill’s new book is devoted.


In

 Requiem for French Theory: Transatlantic Funeral Dirge in a Marxist Key

 (New York,

Monthly Review Press

, 2026, $22.00, 168 pp.), Monville and Rockhill show that what became known as “French Theory” in the US was both a calculated interruption of the rediscovery and study of Marxism and an intellectual trend hostile to anti-capitalist and socialist currents….”

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”


Spaulding wrote in a public FAQ posted on the local’s social media that the temporary administration “is not intended to be punitive or find guilt against any individual in the Local. It is intended to stabilize the Local while issues are …

author: By Niko Georgiades, Unicorn Riot
title: Minneapolis March Against Police Brutality Connects Local, State and Federal Violence
content:
Minneapolis, MN — For the 31st annual National Day of Protest Against Police Brutality on Oct. 22, activists drew the connection to the violence perpetrated by local, state, and federal law enforcement as they marched from the memorial site of

Alex Pretti

 to

Renée Good

‘s memorial and ended at

George Floyd Square

.


Organizing the march for the twenty-sixth straight year was

Communities United Against Police Brutality

 (

CUAPB

). “We want to draw the lines, make the connections, help people understand that it does not matter whether that brutality is by a local law enforcement, a county law enforcement, a state police, or the federal law enforcement. It doesn’t matter when somebody loses their lives to police brutality, misconduct, and abuse of authority. We will always be out here demanding justice. That will never change,” said Michelle Gross, the president of CUAPB.


Before the march started from Alex Pretti’s memorial at 26th St. and Nicollet Ave.,

Brass Solidarity band

 got the crowd moving and singing along to their resistance songs. In attendance for the action were several impacted families and friends of families with stolen lives, including, but not limited to,

Tekle Sundberg

 (Minneapolis Police),

Paul Castaway

 (Denver Police) and

Kobe Heisler

 (Brooklyn Center Police).


Toshira Garraway, whose fiancé

Justin Teigen was found dead in a recycling center

 after an interaction with the St. Paul Police in 2009, spoke at the rally and reminded the crowd that before the deadly Operation Metro Surge, Minnesota police have been deadly.


“Let’s think about the brutality and the evil and the corruption that we were facing right here in Minnesota by our local law enforcement before the Ice agents even showed up,” said Garraway, “and then the ICE agents showed us up and brutalized us even more.”


After marching to Good’s memorial on 33rd St. and Portland Ave., activist Jae Yates noted that Good’s “identity was erased repeatedly after she was killed. Nobody wanted to talk about the fact that this is also violence against the queer community,” they said, “that this is violence against a queer mom who moved here specifically for the safety that she thought that she would find in Minneapolis.”


“This is what we mean when we say all of these struggles are connected. Because if you can murder a white queer woman in the street. What do you think is happening to Black and brown people? If you can kill a Native woman [

Allison Lussier

], not investigate her death, and then face zero consequences within your department? What do you think is happening to the rest of your neighbors?”


Jae Yates


Also at Good’s memorial, Jaylani Hussein, the Executive Director of the Minnesota Chapter of the Council on American-Islamic Relations (

CAIR-MN

) reminded the crowd of the collective power that the Twin Cities community showed to push out the federal occupation.


Hussein noted that it was Minneapolis neighbors looking out for their neighbors like Renée Good “who stood on the streets with their whistles and with their phones,” that got Greg Bovino, the former “commander at large” of the Border Patrol and Kristi Noem, the former Homeland Security Secretary, fired. He implored Minnesotans never forget what happened and to continue to make strides toward justice.


The march ended at George Floyd Square where the community met at independent photojournalist

KingDemetrius Pendleton

‘s

Listen 2 Us Studio

 on 37th St. and Chicago Ave for refreshments and rides back to the march’s starting point.

author: Pinko Collective
title: Letter in Support of the Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá and Trans and Queer People Facing State Repression Worldwide
content:
We reprint the open letter below in support of the Dolls of Berlin. To add your name as a signatory, follow the link at the bottom of the page.

On the afternoon of Sunday 18 October a large police squad forcibly entered Casa Kuá, a queer community center in Berlin, Germany, where at that point The Dolls of Berlin, a transfem social collective, was gathering. Police detained several women for hours while ransacking Casa Kuá. We, the undersigned, stand in support with The Dolls of Berlin, Casa Kuá, and queer and trans people facing state violence, repression and erasure everywhere. We are demanding that the German State drop the case and immediately stop the criminalization of trans spaces and solidarities. We are urging everyone to contribute to the fundraiser, to help our comrades continue their essential work and activities, and keep

nourishing much needed survival spaces for the most vulnerable communities

. 

The attack against the Berlin Dolls comes at a time of unprecedented rise of state fascism, both in Germany where the AfD recently won local elections in Saxony-Anhalt, in neighbouring European countries, and in India, Brazil, Argentina, the United States and elsewhere. This rise of the far right has been accompanied by a massive increase on attacks on queer and trans people. In Turkey between 12-14 September, in coordinated overnight raids across five cities, Turkish police targeted seven LGBTQI+ rights organizations, two groups supporting people living with HIV, and 13 bars and clubs where queer people gather. Board members of some of the country’s oldest LGBTQI+ associations, including Kaos GL and Lambda Istanbul, were

taken from their homes

. Human Rights Watch reports that at least

112 people were arrested and that 82 remain in detention

 by court order. On 3/4 October Taiwan police

raided a Taipei queer bar

 detaining 51 persons and abusing disabled customers.

At the same time, increasingly authoritarian states, including Germany, are seeking to erase trans existence through administrative violence, putting barriers in front of access to trans healthcare. As European governments divert public spending to remilitarisation efforts, access to housing, welfare, jobs and education become circumscribed. In the UK, the drastically curtailed access to trans healthcare in recent years has led to trans suicides on an

unprecedented scale

. Recent government guidelines on so-called 'single sex spaces' are likely to cause more deaths such as that of trans woman, Joelle, who died after being

denied cancer care for 16 days

. A stark example of the hypocrisy on the part of the ruling elite came on 21 October when openly gay Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jette and his partner celebrated the expected arrival of their child, while his government

denies queer refugees the right to family reunification

. The attacks on queer and trans people are accompanied by attacks on, and further marginalisation of the disabled, migrants and refugees, precarious workers, poor Black, Brown and Indigenous communities, the unhoused and incarcerated, compounded for those in multiple of these categories. It is a tell-tale sign of fascism when particular communities are rendered vulnerable, disposable and presented as scapegoats for the various harmful effects of racialised capitalism. 

That the relatively small community of queer and trans people, and racialised trans femmes in particular, has become a target for (proto-)fascist and authoritarian regimes globally is no surprise. Transness especially stands out as a visible transgression of cis hetero patriarchal norms on which fascist authority is built. It forms a thorn in the eye of regimes dependent on popular internalisation of its structural "truths". Transness thus becomes a powerful wedge issue that allows states to whip up fear and distrust of trans people which is consolidated through state carceral and administrative violence. It is also no surprise that state attacks on queer and trans people are on the rise globally at a time when Gen Z, along with older social movements are rising up in France, Albania, Brazil, India, Argentina, Indonesia, Greece and across the planet. Time and again, queer and trans people have stood at the helm of

social movements and popular struggles for liberation

.


The 18 October attack on The Dolls of Berlin at Casa Kuá is historic. Coming at this conjuncture in history, it is signaling the moment that demands we all stand up not only …

author: rezgar2
title: The Brazilian Victory: Left Unity and Digital Autonomy
content:
Rezgar Akrawi : Lula's victory offers an experience worth studying and learning from. It demonstrates the possibility of cooperation among left-wing forces despite their differences, while recognizing the other factors that contributed to the result.


The left does not need to erase its diversity in order to unite. It needs to turn that diversity into an organized and effective force, strengthen its independence across all five pillars, and pursue the struggle for freedom, equality, and social justice while developing democratic, humanist socialist alternatives to capitalism.


Author


Rezgar Akrawi


رزكار عقراوي


    Submitted by

rezgar2

 on October 29, 2026


Rezgar Akrawi


The leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic victory in Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026. The result came amid intense political and social polarization and the growing influence of the far right in Brazil and across Latin America, backed by the American far right led by Donald Trump.


The significance of this electoral victory extends beyond Lula securing a fourth term. It also lies in the political and organizational experience that helped make it possible, above all the ability of diverse left-wing and progressive forces, with different programs and ideological outlooks, to forge a broad electoral alliance around common ground in confronting the far right.


A Broad Left-Wing and Progressive Alliance Despite Differences


Lula contested the election with the support of the ‘Brazil Ready for More’ alliance, comprising seven left-wing and progressive parties organized into two party federations and two separate parties. The ‘Brazil of Hope’ federation brought together Lula’s Workers’ Party, the Communist Party of Brazil, and the Green Party. The second federation united the Socialism and Liberty Party, which includes socialist and radical-left currents, with the Sustainability Network. The Brazilian Socialist Party and the Democratic Labour Party also joined the alliance, alongside supportive social movements and trade unions. Lula ran with Geraldo Alckmin of the Brazilian Socialist Party as his vice-presidential candidate.


The importance of this alliance lies in its ability to bring together communists, socialists, the radical left, social democrats, and Greens despite their disagreements over capitalism, the role of the state, and the limits of social reform. These forces agreed on common electoral objectives while preserving their identities and organizational autonomy.


This is one of the most important lessons of the Brazilian experience. Left unity does not require ideological or organizational uniformity. It means being able to work together on common ground while respecting pluralism and differences.

 Disagreements over Lula’s economic and social policies will naturally persist, including among the forces that supported him at the ballot box.


Unity Does Not Mean Abandoning Criticism or Autonomy


The Brazilian experience raises an important question for left-wing forces around the world. Why do ideological and organizational differences become barriers to cooperation, despite so much common ground, even when these forces face shared political and class challenges?


Pluralism among communists, social democrats, the radical left, environmentalist and feminist currents, and independent leftists can be a source of strength and intellectual and political richness, provided it is managed democratically and constructively, without monopolization, exclusion, or claims to possess the absolute truth.

 Unity does not require abandoning criticism or offering unconditional acceptance of the policies of governments led by left-wing and progressive alliances.


Confronting Capitalism and the Far Right Requires a Broad Social Front


The victory demonstrated the importance of connecting the defense of democracy, rights, and freedoms with the economic and social demands of working classes and poor and marginalized communities.


Lula drew broad support from lower-income groups and proposed expanding social assistance, improving living conditions, and defending democratic institutions.


Confronting capitalism and the far right therefore cannot be confined to elections and party alliances. It requires sustained mass organizations in workplaces, neighborhoods, universities, trade unions, and social movements, together with policies that tackle class inequality and improve the lives of the majority …

author: Mary Stuart
title: How the Far-Right Uses Climate Disasters to Build Political Power
content:
Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s

End Times Fascism and the Fight for the Living World

 is critical reading for anyone seeking to understand and push back against the far-right coalitions wielding considerable state and corporate power around the world.


Klein and Taylor posit that today’s fascists believe that end times have arrived, and have made it their mission to profit from cascading global crises, while hunkering down and protecting themselves as the world burns around them.


The book details three factions of end times fascists, united by their shared apocalypticism. The religious fundamentalists believe end times are upon us, but they will be saved by their messiah. The Silicon Valley technologists are building technologies they say could be world-ending, that in the meantime are killing jobs, consuming vast resources, and polluting communities. The ethno-nationalists espouse conspiratorial ideas about cultural replacement and treat immigration as an existential threat.


DeSmog Canada editor/reporter Mary Stuart spoke with Astra Taylor about how climate change fits into end times fascism, the importance of AI data centre fights, and how we can understand Canadian Prime Minister Carney’s neoliberal moves in response to U.S. President Donald Trump.


Taylor is a writer, documentarian, and activist. She co-founded the

Debt Collective

, a membership-based union for debtors, and is the author of several books, including

The Age of Insecurity

 and

Democracy May Not Exist But We’ll Miss It When It is Gone

.


This interview was conducted by phone and has been edited for length and clarity.


Mary Stuart:

 

I


want to start by


asking how your book can help us understand some recent elections. Jair Bolsonaro’s son Flávio won the first round of voting in Brazil’s election and


nearly


became president. The far-right AfD recently won in Saxony-Anhalt.


How do these wins fit into your analysis of end times fascism?


Astra Taylor:

 One phenomena we describe in End Times Fascism relevant here is the role of Pentecostal religious communities in turning out the vote. To paraphrase reporting from Brazil, a voter said “my heart’s with Lula, but my pastor told me to vote for Flávio”.


The incredibly difficult conditions that we’re living under created fertile terrain for prophecy and religion, for kinds of pentecostalism, a faith that is focused on prosperity, individual advancement and banking on the idea that life is suffering here on earth, but you will be rewarded in the afterlife.


There’s also interference from Tech oligarchs. We don’t know the half of it at this moment, but the way the platform [Meta] refused to run ads for Lula’s party and beyond is certainly a factor. And the Trump regime [is playing a role] as well.


AfD is a similar. Naomi and I wrote a piece in the

Financial Times

 and we open with the images that went viral this summer of the Danube River drying, and Nazi warships emerging. Hundreds of Nazi warships sank during WWII, and as the river receded, this paraphernalia was coming out of the mud. We thought it was a powerful metaphor for today. What’s really striking is the riverbed— the fact that it’s drying because of climate change. Our point is that fascism always emerges from crises. And we cannot separate the ecological and economic crises people are facing.


People are really struggling with affordability. People are feeling that they don’t have a future. And actually quite strikingly, rates of immigration are quite low, right? So [Saxony-Anhalt is] one of the places with the least immigration, but [the AfD] step in and say “the problem is the immigrants, it’s not a larger economic system.” This is a classic fascist move that we describe throughout the book.


MS:


What role do climate change and climate denial play in end times fascism?


AT:

 Naomi and I are insistent that the planet is a player in our politics. Fascism always surges in moments of crisis.


We are in a world that is being roiled by disasters and shocks. We’ve reached a point where the consequences [of climate change] are undeniable. You cannot deny a heat dome when you’re inside it. You cannot deny a hurricane when it’s blowing the roof off your house. Of course, you can still deny why the storm is coming. You can embrace a Marjorie Taylor Greene perspective and say that it’s due to space lasers or you can say “the climate has always chained, this is nothing new, we don’t know if it’s human causing it.” …

author: Unknown
title: Bolsonaro'nun ABD'ye firarı, sağın Brezilya seçimlerine yönelik iddialarını çaptan düşürdü
content:
Brezilya'da 25 Ekim cumhurbaşkanlığı seçimini kaybeden senatör Flávio Bolsonaro'nun, Yüksek Federal Mahkemenin (STF) yurt dışına çıkış yasağını çiğneyerek ABD'ye kaçışının ayrıntıları, millyetçi adayın bir uluslararası ağın içinde hareket ettiğini belgeliyor.


Brezilya Federal Polisi, mahkeme yasağının nasıl aşıldığını araştırırken Arjantin yargısı da re'sen Javier Milei hükümeti yetkililerinin kaçışa yardımcı olup olmadığını incelemeye başladı.


ABD'de The New York Times, Bolsonaro'yu Arjantin'den Miami'ye taşıyan özel uçağın Beyaz Saray'da görevli Jason Miller tarafından ayarlandığını bildirdi. Gazeteye göre Trump yönetimi, Bolsonaro ve ailesinin ülkeye girişi için özel bir göçmenlik statüsünü işletti. 


Önce "kalacağım" dedi... 


Bolsonaro hakkındaki yurt dışına çıkış yasağı, Federal Polisin 25 Ekim'deki başvurusu üzerine STF yargıcı Alexandre de Moraes tarafından karara bağlandı.


Federal Polis, Bolsonaro'nun ülkeyi terk etme riski bulunduğunu belirterek pasaportlarına el konulmasını, diğer şüphelilerle iletişiminin sınırlandırılmasını ve yurt dışına çıkışının yasaklanmasını istemişti.


Bolsonaro'ya 26 Ekim Pazartesi sabahı, Brezilya pasaportlarının yanı sıra varsa başka ülkelere ait pasaportlarını da 24 saat içinde teslim etmesi bildirildi.


Senatör aynı gün sosyal medyada yayımladığı videoda şöyle demişti:


"Ülkeden ayrılmayı hiçbir zaman düşünmedim. Pasaportlarımı teslim edeceğim ve beni yıldırmaya yönelik açık bir girişim olan bu saçmalığa karşı kendimi savunacağım."


Ancak Bolsonaro pasaportlarını teslim etmediği gibi ertesi gece ailesiyle birlikte Brezilya'dan ayrıldı.


Federal Polis, normal ve diplomatik Brezilya


pasaportlarını iptal etti ve sınır kontrol sistemi SONAR'a uyarı kaydı yerleştirdi.


Kurumun 28 Ekim tarihli açıklamasına göre Bolsonaro'nun ülkeyi terk ederken Brezilya göç kontrol noktalarından geçtiğine ilişkin hiçbir resmî kayıt bulunmuyor.


İtalyan pasaportuyla Arjantin'e, özel uçakla Miami'ye


Arjantin Göç İdaresi'nin doğruladığı bilgilere göre Bolsonaro, eşi Fernanda ve iki kızıyla birlikte 27 Ekim Salı günü saat 22.50'de Foz do Iguaçu ile Puerto Iguazú arasındaki Tancredo Neves Uluslararası Köprüsü'nden Arjantin'e girdi.


Bolsonaro'nun Arjantin makamlarına İtalyan pasaportunu gösterdiği, ailesinin ise Brezilya belgelerini kullandığı belirlendi.


Aile, Puerto Iguazú Havaalanı'nda bekleyen Baires Fly şirketine ait Gulfstream G400 tipi özel uçağa bindi. Uçak 28 Ekim'in ilk saatlerinde havalanarak Ekvador'un Guayaquil kentine gitti. Burada yakıt ikmalinin ardından uçuşunu Miami istikametinde sürdürdü.


Uçuş güzergâhı Brezilya hava sahasına girmeksizin yola devam edeceği biçimde düzenlenmişti. Uçak 28 Ekim Çarşamba günü Brezilya saatiyle 10.23'te ABD'de Miami yakınındaki Opa-locka Executive Airport'a indi.


Bolsonaro'nun Brasília'dan Arjantin sınırına nasıl ulaştığı ise henüz bütünüyle aydınlatılmış değil.


Özel uçağı Trump'ın danışmanı mı ayarladı?


The New York Times'ın 29 Ekim tarihli haberine göre yolculukta kullanılan özel uçak, Trump yönetiminde iletişim alanında görev yapan Jason Miller tarafından ayarlandı.


Gazetenin, operasyonun lojistiğinden haberdar olan bir kaynağa dayandırdığı haberde, Bolsonaro'nun ABD'de yaşayan kardeşi Eduardo'nun Miller ile temas halinde olduğu ve planın, pasaport teslimi kararının ardından uygulamaya konulduğu belirtildi.


Miller konuyla ilgili açıklama yapmayı reddetti. Beyaz Saray ise uçağın ayarlanmasına ilişkin soruları yanıtlamak yerine Trump'ın medyaya verdiği demeçlere göndermede bulundu. 


Trump, Bolsonaro'nun ABD'ye kabul edilmesi konusu şöyle dedi: 


"Ülkeye girmesi için ona izin verdik. Bundan sonra ne olacağını göreceğiz. Ama bu işe karışmayacağım."


New York Times'a konuşan Amerikalı yetkililer, Bolsonaro ve ailesinin ülkeye olağan yolcu vizesiyle değil, 

parole

 adı verilen özel ve geçici kabul statüsüyle alındığını bildirdiler.


Bu statü ABD makamlarına belirli insani gerekçeler veya kamu yararı gerekçesiyle kişilere geçici giriş izni verme yetkisi tanıyor. Siyasi sığınma kararıyla aynı anlama gelmiyor.


Gazeteye göre Bolsonaro'nun daha sonra kalıcı oturma iznine başvurması da öngörülüyor.


Arjantin'de Milei'nin danışmanının rolü araştırılıyor


Firarın Arjantin ayağında ise kurumsal bir adli süreç başlatıldı.


La Nación gazetesinin 29 Ekim tarihli haberine göre federal yargıç María Eugenia Capuchetti, Bolsonaro'nun sınır geçişi ve Puerto Iguazú Havaalanı'ndan ayrılışına ilişkin görüntü kayıtlarının korunmasını …

author: infolibre
title: ΝΙΚΟΣ ΜΑΖΙΩΤΗΣ: Ο απολογισμός ενός αντάρτη πόλης
content:
Ο ΑΠΟΛΟΓΙΣΜΟΣ ΕΝΟΣ ΑΝΤΑΡΤΗ ΠΟΛΗΣ


Μετά από 14 χρόνια στη φυλακή για τη δράση του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα έφτασα στο τέλος μιας μεγάλης και σκληρής δοκιμασίας.


Το να είναι κανείς επαναστάτρια/επαναστάτης αποδεικνύεται από το κόστος των επιλογών που διατίθεται να πληρώσει και από την υπεράσπιση των επιλογών αγώνα για τις οποίες βρέθηκε στη φυλακή.


Στην περίπτωσή μας, μια μακροχρόνια φυλάκιση ή ο θάνατος σε μια συμπλοκή με τους υπηρέτες του κράτους και των αφεντικών, όπως έγινε με τον σύντροφο Λάμπρο Φούντα στις 10 Μαρτίου 2010, είναι το αντίτιμο των επιλογών μας, κάτι που γνώριζα εξαρχής.


Στον αγώνα όπως και στη ζωή γενικά, τίποτα δεν υπάρχει χωρίς αντίτιμο. Γιατί ό,τι αξίζει είναι δύσκολο και απαιτεί θυσίες.


Το κόστος των επιλογών όμως ισχύει για όλους ανεξαιρέτως, ακόμα και για τον εχθρό, όπως και για τους υπηρέτες του κράτους που τραυματίστηκαν από τα όπλα του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα, στα Εξάρχεια το 2009 μετά την δολοφονία του Γρηγορόπουλου, στην απαλλοτρίωση της τράπεζας Πειραιώς στην Κλειτορία το 2014, στο Μοναστηράκι επίσης το 2014 που παραλίγο να με σκοτώσουν.


Για αρκετά χρόνια, οι δομές και οι μηχανισμοί του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου γνώρισαν την ισχύ των βομβών του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα, όπως το παράρτημα της ΕΚΤ, η Τράπεζα της Ελλάδας και το γραφείο του ΔΝΤ, το Χρηματιστήριο Αθηνών, τα υπουργεία Απασχόλησης και Οικονομίας, τα δικαστήρια της Ευελπίδων, αστυνομικά τμήματα όπως της Καλλιθέας και του Περισσού, τράπεζες όπως η Citibank και η Eurobank. Φυσικά οι ΗΠΑ δεν θα ξεχάσουν ποτέ την επίθεση με αντιαρματική ρουκέτα στην πρεσβεία τους στην Αθήνα το 2007. Ενώ ο πρώην υπουργός Δημόσιας Τάξης, Βουλγαράκης, αντιλήφθηκε ότι κανείς κυβερνητικός αξιωματούχος, όσο υψηλόβαθμος κι αν είναι, δεν είναι αλώβητος.


Ο Επαναστατικός Αγώνας είναι κομμάτι μιας ιστορικής παράδοσης μέσα στο επαναστατικό και αναρχικό κίνημα από την εποχή της Α΄ Διεθνούς Ένωσης Εργατών που χρησιμοποίησε τον ένοπλο αγώνα και την πρακτική του αντάρτικου όπως έκανε η οργάνωση Ναρόντναγια Βόλια (Λαϊκή Θέληση) στη Ρωσία ή όπως έκαναν οι αναρχικοί με αυτό που ονόμαζαν «προπαγάνδα με την πράξη» όταν πραγματοποιούσαν βομβιστικές επιθέσεις και εκτελέσεις βασιλιάδων, προέδρων κρατών, πρωθυπουργών. Είναι κομμάτι μιας ιστορικής παράδοσης που συστατικά της μέρη ήταν η αντιφρανκική ένοπλη αντίσταση, το αντάρτικο κατά των δυνάμεων του Άξονα στην κατεχόμενη Ευρώπη, το αντάρτικο πόλης των τελευταίων δεκαετιών.


Ο Επαναστατικός Αγώνας είναι κομμάτι μιας ιστορικής παράδοσης που βασίζεται στους αγώνες των λαών για την κοινωνική απελευθέρωση από τον ζυγό του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου, για αυτοοργάνωση ενάντια στο συγκεντρωτικό κράτος όποια μορφή και αν έχει αυτό. Μιας παράδοσης που βασίζεται μεταξύ άλλων στην Παρισινή Κομμούνα του 1871, την αντικρατική τάση της Ρωσικής Επανάστασης –όπως την Κομμούνα της Κρονστάνδης του 1921 και την Μαχνοφτσίνα (1918-’21) στην Ουκρανία που αγωνίστηκε εναντίον των τσαρικών λευκών αντεπαναστατών, των εθνικιστών και του ανερχόμενου μπολσεβίκικου ολοκληρωτισμού–, τη Μεξικανική Επανάσταση και την Ισπανική Επανάσταση (1936-’39) που δολοφονήθηκε τόσο από τους σταλινικούς αντεπαναστάτες όσο και τους φρανκικούς φασίστες.


Στη διαδρομή της αγωνιστικής ζωής μου έχω περάσει 18 χρόνια στις φυλακές για τις επιλογές μου που τις τίμησα και τις υπερασπίστηκα δημόσια στην κοινωνία και μπροστά στον εχθρό. Από αυτά τα 18 χρόνια, τα 14 χρόνια είναι για τη δράση του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα. Όσο παράδοξο και αν φαίνεται σε κάποιους ίσως, οι αγωνιστές της ελευθερίας αγαπούν τη ζωή παθιασμένα ρισκάροντας μερικές φορές να σκοτωθούν ενώ αγαπούν την ελευθερία ρισκάροντας να βρεθούν στη φυλακή.


Η ίδρυση του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα το 2003 και η συμμετοχή μου σ’ αυτόν ήταν το αποτέλεσμα μιας αγωνιστικής και πολιτικής ωρίμανσης. Από αυτή τη δοκιμασία βγαίνω, όπως βγήκε και η συντρόφισσα Ρούπα, νικητής με το κεφάλι ψηλά. Γιατί υπερασπιστήκαμε την πολιτική μας ταυτότητα ως μέλη του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα. Γιατί υπερασπιστήκαμε τη δράση μας και όλες τις επιθέσεις του Επαναστατικού Αγώνα, μία προς μία, και τις 18 ενέργειες από το 2003 ως το 2017, σε όλες τις δίκες εναντίον της οργάνωσης. Γιατί υπερασπιστήκαμε τον σύντροφό μας Λάμπρο Φούντα, μέλος της οργάνωσης που σκοτώθηκε σε συμπλοκή με αστυνομικούς. Γιατί αν είχαμε απαρνηθεί την πολιτική μας ταυτότητα με την ελπίδα να σωθούμε από την καταστολή, αν δεν είχαμε αναλάβει την πολιτική ευθύνη, αυτό θα ήταν η ύψιστη μορφή αλλοτρίωσης, θα είχαμε προδώσει τον νεκρό σύντροφό μας Λάμπρο Φούντα που σκοτώθηκε σε προπαρασκευαστική …

author: Unknown
title: Yuossef Siher, il primo detenuto politico della magistratura predittiva italiana
content:
Riprendiamo questa interessante analisi di McSilvan apparsa su

Codice Rosso

 per restituire una chiave di lettura della vicenda legata a Youssef Siher.


L’ordinamento penale costituzionale italiano si fonda sul principio di materialità e di offensività del fatto (artt. 25, comma 2, e 27 della Costituzione): il soggetto può essere assoggettato a sanzione o a restrizione della libertà personale esclusivamente in ragione di una condotta che leda o ponga in

pericolo concreto

 un bene giuridico tutelato. Tuttavia, quando si tratta di “terrorismo” o di “eversione dell’ordine democratico”, si assiste a una progressiva, perversa torsione del paradigma punitivo e cautelare.


Infatti, nei procedimenti per reati associativi o istigatori aggravati dalla finalità di terrorismo, il trattenimento in custodia cautelare in carcere

 cessa di dipendere dalla gravità oggettiva

 e dalla consistenza offensiva del fatto commesso, per ancorarsi in via preminente alla 

potenzialità lesiva ed eversiva della persona

, estesa dagli organi inquirenti fino al massimo grado consentito dall’interpretazione prognostica della biografia, del capitale culturale e delle competenze tecniche dell’indagato.


Il caso giudiziario di Youssef Siher — sottoposto a fermo di indiziato di delitto dalla Procura della Repubblica di Milano il 24 ottobre 2026 in seguito alla creazione dei canali social denominati “Movimento 17 ottobre” — costituisce un caso di studio paradigmatico. L’esame congiunto degli atti d’indagine, della costruzione mediatica del caso, dell’evoluzione legislativa del decennio 2015–2026 e dell’impiego delle tecnologie di intelligenza artificiale dimostrano come l’apparato repressivo tenda oggi a neutralizzare 

preventivamente

 la capacità intellettuale e relazionale del soggetto, surrogando con essa la mancanza di offensività materiale della condotta. In poche parole, la 

magistratura sanziona perché si fa predittiva

 e, in materia di “terrorismo”, Youssif Siher segna il non invidiabile record di 

primo detenuto

 

politico 

di questo genere di magistratura.


1. Youssif Siher, il profilo


Youssef Siher è un cittadino italiano di 30 anni, cosiddetto di seconda generazione, nato nel bresciano da famiglia di origini marocchine, anagraficamente residente a Mazzano (Brescia) e domiciliato di fatto nell’area metropolitana milanese. Sotto il profilo linguistico e culturale, è bilingue (madrelingua italiano e arabo) e parla fluentemente inglese e spagnolo.


Il suo percorso accademico si è sviluppato interamente presso l’Università degli Studi di Milano (Statale), dove ha conseguito nel luglio 2020 la laurea triennale in Comunicazione — discutendo con il professor Nicola Del Corno una tesi storiografica in Storia delle dottrine politiche sulla 

Sunna

e sulla recezione dei precetti islamici nelle istituzioni statuali, giudicata dal relatore priva di connotazione radicale o apologetica — e successivamente la laurea magistrale in Scienze Politiche, con una tesi sui movimenti islamici in Marocco e i loro rapporti con la monarchia. Durante gli anni universitari è stato eletto rappresentante degli studenti nel Senato Accademico nelle liste di 

UniLab

, formazione studentesca di orientamento moderato e vicina al centrodestra. Nel 2024 ha svolto un tirocinio di ricerca (

research trainee

) presso l’Osservatorio sul Medio Oriente e Nord Africa dell’ISPI (Istituto per gli Studi di Politica Internazionale).


Sul piano lavorativo, ha operato come giornalista freelance collaborando con 

Il Fatto Quotidiano

(occupandosi tra il 2022 e il 2024 di proteste studentesche e poi di crisi internazionali in Tunisia, Egitto, Sudan, Gaza e Mar Rosso), con 

Il Foglio

 (un singolo articolo sul Pakistan nel 2022) e con il canale satellitare panarabo 

Al Mayadeen English

, ritenuto politicamente contiguo a Hezbollah. Da gennaio 2026 lavora come esperto generalista per 

Mercor

, una startup statunitense di intelligenza artificiale, occupandosi di valutazione, etichettatura dati (

data labeling

) e addestramento di modelli algoritmici. Nel 2024 era stato oggetto di una segnalazione dei servizi di intelligence italiani per aver fondato e presieduto l’associazione 

Organizzazione Alba Nascente

 (OAN), attiva nel contrasto all’islamofobia e nelle mobilitazioni pro-Palestina. Nel settembre 2026 ha si è sposato con Sagia Hammoud, trentaduenne mediatrice interculturale nata e residente a Como, di origini libanesi e palestinesi, attivista dei  …

author: Unknown
title: Суд в Финляндии утвердил отказ Миграционной службы предоставить убежище 44-летнему анархисту из Петербурга Михаилу Луньковскому
content:
Об этом написала «Медиазона». Фотографию Луньковского также публикует издание.

Его постановили депортировать в Россию.

Луньковский рассказал «Медиазоне», что в самом начале войны он отправлял деньги в украинские фонды вроде «Повернись живим» с российских карт. Он открыто выступал против вторжения и оставлял антивоенные комментарии в различных чатах в телеграме.

С 2017-2018 годов, по словам Луньковского, и по настоящее время он занимается модерацией в чате преследуемого в РФ и жёстко критикующего Путина публициста Аркадия Бабченко. В последние годы несколько человек получили большие сроки за донаты Бабченко.

По версии финского суда, «деятельность заявителя в социальных сетях носила весьма незначительный характер». Суд не нашел подтверждений, что «заявитель представляет особый интерес для российских властей».

По данным Автономного Действия, Луньковский был активен в питерских либертарных инициативах в 2000-х годов. Решение суда в Финляндии попытаются оспорить.

author: Perseus
title: “Δεν υπήρχε σπιθαμή στο σώμα του που να μην ήταν χτυπημένη” – Πώς η δικαιοσύνη επιβραβεύει την αστυνομική βία
content:
“Δεν υπήρχε σπιθαμή στο σώμα του που να μην ήταν χτυπημένη” – Πώς η δικαιοσύνη επιβραβεύει την αστυνομική βία


Στις 21 Σεπτεμβρίου 2024, ο Μοχάμεντ

Καμράν

 Ασίκ δολοφονήθηκε από αστυνομικούς στο Α.Τ. Αγίου Παντελεήμονα. Τον Ιανουάριο του 2026, ο εισαγγελέας Σωτήρης Μπουγιούκος αποφάσισε να αρχειοθετήσει την υπόθεση, ισχυριζόμενος ότι δεν υπήρχαν επαρκή στοιχεία για να παραπεμφθεί σε δίκη. Ως αποτέλεσμα, δεν υπάρχουν πλέον νομικά μέσα για τη συνέχιση της υπόθεσης στα ελληνικά δικαστήρια. Οι αστυνομικοί που τον ξυλοκόπησαν μέχρι θανάτου συνεχίζουν τη ζωή τους χωρίς καμία συνέπεια.


Ο Μοχάμεντ Καμράν Ασίκ, εργάτης από το Πακιστάν, συνελήφθη, μεταφέρθηκε και κρατήθηκε σε πέντε διαδοχικά αστυνομικά τμήματα, όπου υπέστη επανειλημμένη σωματική βία, χωρίς ουσιαστική επικοινωνία με την οικογένειά του ή πρόσβαση σε νομική υποστήριξη. Στις 21 Σεπτεμβρίου 2024 βρέθηκε νεκρός μέσα στο Αστυνομικό Τμήμα Αγίου Παντελεήμονα, στον μοναδικό χώρο που δεν είχε κάλυψη από κάμερες. Ακόμα και η ίδια η κρατική ιατροδικαστική πραγματογνωμοσύνη κατέληξε στο συμπέρασμα ότι ο θάνατός του προκλήθηκε από ισχαιμία του μυοκαρδίου, ως αποτέλεσμα έντονου σωματικού και ψυχικού στρες που συνδέεται με τον συνεχή ξυλοδαρμό κατά την κράτησή του.


Τη δολοφονία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν ακολούθησε εκτεταμένη συγκάλυψη της υπόθεσης (όπως τέτοια ακολούθησε και το κρατικό έγκλημα στην Πύλο). Οι αστυνομικοί του Α.Τ. Αγίου Παντελεήμονα ισχυρίστηκαν ότι «αυτοτραυματίστηκε λόγω στερητικού συνδρόμου αλκοόλ». Ο εισαγγελέας Σωτήρης Μπουγιούκος πολύ στοχευμένα παρέλειψε στην επίσημη αναφορά το ιατρικό συμπέρασμα που ξεκάθαρα αποδίδει την καρδιακή αποτυχία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν ως αποτέλεσμα του εκτεταμένου και άγριου ξυλοδαρμού του. Αυτή η απόφαση είναι ξεδιάντροπη συγκάλυψη του βασανισμού και της δολοφονίας του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν από την ελληνική αστυνομία.


(Ενημερωτικό απόσπασμα από το κάλεσμα της Ανοιχτής Συνέλευση Ενάντια στην Κρατική Δολοφονία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν σε πορεία για τα 2 χρόνια από τη δολοφονία του Καμράν)


Οι ζωές μας στις γειτονιές της Αθήνας γίνονται καθημερινά όλο και πιο ασφυκτικές μέσα σε ένα κλίμα κρατικής βίας, εκφοβισμού και πρακτικών συνεχούς επιτήρησης.


Η κρατική εξουσία μέσω νεοφιλελεύθερων πολιτικών πασχίζει να εδραιώσει και να φυσικοποιήσει πρακτικέςπεριθωριοποίησης και εκτοπισμού αυτών των ομάδων που αντιστέκονται καιεναντιώνονται στην απαξίωση των ζωών τους. Η καπιταλιστική πολιτική «ανάπτυξης» στη συνέχεια στοχεύει στην διάλυση και στον αφανισμό κάθε είδους κοινότητας και συλλογικοποίησης. Προσπαθεί να δημιουργήσει γειτονιές απονέκρωσης, φόβου, αποσιώπησης και υποταγής χτυπώντας στους κατεξοχήν τόπους συγκέντρωσης, μοιράσματος και ζύμωσης: τις πλατείες.


Η πλατεία Βικτωρίας αποτελεί εδώ και πολλά χρόνια ένα πεδίο μάχης και συλλογικών αγώνων. Οι γειτονιές κάτω από την Πατησίων είναι ο επόμενος στόχος της λεγόμενης “ανάπλασης”, ενός σχεδίου που υπόσχεται “αναβάθμιση των ζωών”, αλλά στην πράξη συχνά μεταφράζεται σε αποκλεισμό, εμπορευματοποίηση και έλεγχο του δημόσιου χώρου. Από τα pushbacks και τα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης, από τη θάλασσα και τα χερσαία σύνορα μέχρι τις φυλακές και το δημόσιο χώρο, το κράτος δείχνει το ρατσιστικό του πρόσωπο. Μέσα σε ένα σκηνικό συνεχών ελέγχων, τραμπουκισμού, ξυλοδαρμών, συλλήψεων και βασανισμών, τα περιστατικά αστυνομικής βίας και κρατικών δολοφονιών μόνο αυξάνονται. Θοδωρής Ζαβραδινός, Κώστας Μανιουδάκης, Ζάκι, Βασίλης Μάγγος, Σαμπάνης, Κώστας Φραγκούλης , Μία Χαριζούλ , Εμπουκά Μαμάν Σούμπεκ, Μοχάμεντ Καμράν, βιασμός 19χρονης στο Α.Τ Ομονοίας και τόσα ακόμα περιστατικά κρατικής τρομοκρατίας που δεν έχουν καταγραφεί.


Η Βικτώρια είναι μια γειτονιά μεταναστευτική, ζωντανή, γεμάτη ιστορίες και πολιτισμούς. Οι άνθρωποι της προσπαθούν καθημερινά να πάρουν ανάσες ελευθερίας, μέσα σε ένα κλίμα αυξανόμενης και ασφυκτικής αστυνομικής παρουσίας.


Δεν είναι δύσκολο να θυμηθούμε κάποιες από τις εικόνες των προηγούμενων χρόνων: τις σκηνές των προσφύγων στην πλατεία, το κύμα αλληλεγγύης που απλώθηκε αυθόρμητα, τα ξηλωμένα παγκάκια και τα κάγκελα που τοποθετήθηκαν για να μην κοιμούνται προσφύγισσες, πρόσφυγες και μετανάστες, τις ρατσιστικές επιχειρήσεις-σκούπα, τους ελέγχους για χαρτιά. Μέσα σε αυτό το κλίμα όμως άνθισαν παρεμβάσεις απέναντι στην καταστολή, το ρατσισμό, την ομοφοβία και την κρατική βία. Μικροφωνικές επανοικειοποίησης, πορείες, παρουσία κοινωνικών ιατρείων, κινήσεις γειτονιάς που αντιστάθηκαν στη σιωπή. title: Dress code Halloween
content:
Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. C'est la première fois que la révolution s'apparente à la chorégraphie du Thriller de Michaël Jackson. Si le Gilet Jaune de 2018 s'est ajouté au k-way noir de 2016, désormais : c'est l'intégralité du multiverse qui se fait costume. Il n'est pas certain que, dans cette immense Battle d'aura avec le gouvernement, ce soient la police qui ait le meilleur déguisement. Joyeux Halloween.

author: Anele Mbi
title: Buffalo City’s broken houses and decades of empty promises
content:
A housing rectification project in Braelyn Extension 10 in Buffalo City Municipality (BCM) has left residents frustrated with the municipality’s failure to address severe structural faults.


Serious defects in the RD houses include cracked walls and roofs, leaking roofs, and inadequate foundations. Braelyn residents say they have repeatedly complained to the municipality, which has promised to rebuild the houses since 2004, but has taken no action until today, except for a laydown yard constructed by the sitting, ANC ward councillor, Mendi Wetsetse.


The stalled housing project intersects with service-delivery defects across the ward, including unpaved and potholed roads, poor refuse collection, and electricity shortages brought about by the growing Inkandla informal settlement.


Recently, President Cyril Ramaphosa authorised the Special Investigating Unit (SIU) to probe allegations of extensive corruption and maladministration of major BCM tenders.


According to Braelyn residents, talks about rectifying Braelyn Ext 10 RDP houses began before 2010. The then ward councillor, Thabo Myira, who served as a councillor between 2005 and 2010, confirmed the claim.


Media reports also indicate that in 2009, the then minister of human settlements, Tokyo Sexwale promised people living in faulty RDP houses in East London that their houses would be rebuilt. Today, councillor Wetsetse, who is campaigning for a third term in the upcoming local government election, promised to rectify the situation.


Housing defects


Ntombizanele Mabala, an 80-year-old pensioner, said since residents arrived in Braelyn in 1997, they have complained to councillors and the municipality about the poor condition of their houses, but their pleas were ignored. “These are not houses but hokkies. We have children and a family of six. Rain comes in from every direction – through the roof, the walls and underneath – because these houses have no foundations,” she said. “The councillor promised that the housing rectification process would begin before 4 November, but there are still no signs of work apart from a laydown-yard fence erected two years ago.”


Another pensioner, Nothembile Mqhayi, whose house was built below ground level, said her house floods when it rains. She showed

Elitsha

 a hole she had made at the bottom of a wall to let water that entered the house drain out.


The Mqhayi family had to make a hole in the wall to drain out water when the house floods.


Ziyanda Mpakantsho (42), who recently joined an EPWP project and earns R3,000 a month, said rectification is urgently needed because she lives with a sick and disabled person. “I grew up hearing that the cracks in the walls would be repaired, but many years have passed. These Braelyn houses have no proper foundations, so water leaks in when it rains. The houses have not been rectified because the money is being squandered,” she said.


Zama Thutha (70) said the government had not fixed the RDP houses because it was corrupt and unaccountable to voters. “Even the EPWP jobs created recently will end after the elections. Our system of government is capitalism, which puts profit before the needs of ordinary people,” he said.


Recurring delays and more promises


Responses from both the BCM and the Eastern Cape department of human settlements (DHS) are not only conflicting but also suggest the rectification process remains a false hope for Braelyn residents. When asked whether the municipality or its ward councillor has made any promises of rectification, the municipality said the provincial government is responsible for the rectification process.


“The Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality wishes to clarify that it does not currently run a municipal housing rectification programme; this falls outside local government funding allocations. What we can say is that the laydown yard established on-site remains a site-securing measure for future development once capital is allocated.”


The laydown yard is overgrown

.


The provincial DHS said that, despite the constitutional principle of cooperative governance that compels the various spheres of government to share information and support each other, implementation requires compliance with the necessary technical, administrative, planning, and budgetary processes. The department has not denied the fact that rectification has been recognised for several years.

author: Alicia Houser
title: Tanzania’s peace was never peaceful
content:
One year ago, on October 29, 2025, the sound of bombs and bullets rang out around Dar es Salaam and several other cities across Tanzania. Before last year’s election, Tanzania had enjoyed an international reputation as a peaceful haven in an often tumultuous region. Foreign governments and tour companies certainly helped craft this image, but so did Tanzania’s government and population. Since I started visiting the country in 2017, people have often cited

amani

 (peace) as one of Tanzania’s best attributes. People attributed this purported peace not to satisfaction with the government or living conditions, but to fear.

Watanzania ni woga

 (Tanzanians are cowards), my friends tell me self-deprecatingly. This fear belies the peaceful image Tanzania has cultivated overseas. 

Histories, or perhaps more accurately colonial histories, place Tanzania in the category of African countries that peacefully acquired independence. To consider Tanzania’s transition to independence as peaceful is to take a short view of history. This narrative ignores the Hehe killed during seven years of fighting against the Germans, which ended in 1898 with

Chief Mkwawa

 killing himself rather than surrendering and his skull being taken to Germany. It ignores the organized resistance that involved the entire southern half of Tanzania, the

Maji Maji

 war of 1905–1908, which some consider the first Pan-African anticolonial resistance movement. The Tanzanian historian Gilbert Gwassa estimated that 300,000 Africans died in this movement, most of them from starvation. The narrative of peaceful transition also ignores the roughly 600,000 Africans who died as a result of

World War I

 military incursions on Tanzanian soil. In these three events alone, almost one million would-be Tanzanians lost their lives to colonization. 

I was in Dar es Salaam last year during the election. The internet cut out at about noon, and the sounds of bombs and bullets started around 1pm and continued off and on for another four days. Without internet, radio, or television, I got my news the old-fashioned way: through other people. My friends in Arusha and Moshi sent frequent messages, and I went out to my courtyard and sat with my neighbors who were connected to other cities across the country. We exchanged what we had heard: someone’s niece had stepped outside her apartment in Dar and encountered a body, Muhimbili Hospital was overflowing, bodies were being stacked outside mortuaries, ballot boxes had been burned. There would be no votes to count. By day three of the lockdown, rumors were circulating that the government was preparing for a prolonged battle, and that Dar’s drinking water might be poisoned. By day five, the store next door to me had sold out of airtime, water, sodas, and milk. Amid the fear, though, was excitement.

Watanzania wameamka,

 one of my neighbors said proudly. Tanzanians have woken up. A neighbor who stopped by noted that

hakuna mafanikio bila

 sacrifice. No success without sacrifice. Another neighbor said she was going to give 10,000 shillings to any

bodaboda

 and

bajaji

 drivers (the motorcycle and three-wheeler taxi drivers who ferry much of urban Tanzania) she saw; they were the ones leading the protests.

On day six, Mama Samia — as President Samia Suluhu Hassan is popularly known — was sworn in as president at a ceremony closed to the public. The sounds of bombs and bullets had fizzled out over the days, and the morning marking one week since the election radiated with the usual city sounds of buses,

bajajis

, and

bodabodas

 that had gone quiet for so long. The halt in violence did not result from any recognition by Samia of the illegitimacy of the election, which did not include any candidates from the country’s main opposition parties. The electoral commission barred Chadema, the largest of them, and disqualified the candidate of ACT-Wazalendo. After days of police shooting

live rounds

 into crowds and indiscriminately killing

civilians

 caught in the wrong place at the wrong time, the protests stopped. Tanzanians decided they did not want to die. After the election, there was a general feeling of “Where do we go from here?”.

Months before the election, in March of last year, I attended a memorial event on the slopes of Mount Kilimanjaro in Old Moshi, remembering the 19 area chiefs whom the Germans hanged on March 2, 1900, on accusations of subversion. One of the elders recalled a phrase he heard often growing …

author: WoMin
title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.

They used them sustainably. So we ask our ancestors to guide us during this Assembly, so that peace and food …

author: Semhal Meles Zenawi
title: Ethiopia: Elections, Constitutional Change, and Genocidal Violence
content:
In November 2020, a war erupted in the Ethiopian region of Tigray. Six hundred thousand to a million civilian lives are estimated to have been lost. Amongst the many war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the two-year war was genocide against Tigrayans. Abiy Ahmed has on several occasions insisted that the catalyst for war was his intolerance for voluntary disassociation and the exercise of the right to vote. 


The National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) postponed the 2020 election several times, but the final “indefinite” postponement under the cover of COVID-19 breached the constitutionally set term limit. Then NEBE chair Birtukan Mideksa’s claim that COVID-19 introduced public health imperatives that overrode those of democracy was unconvincing given the government’s non-enforcement of other measures such as lockdowns or even social distancing, and its farcical claim of having developed a “homegrown” cure. 


Following a public outcry over the “corona-clouded power grab”, four prescriptive options for a “constitutional route to postponement” were presented to a curated array of government-aligned opposition by the then minister of justice, now minister of foreign affairs, Gedion Timothewos. The exercise was met with derision, even by its hand-selected participants. An equally performative constitutional “tribunal” was held, but that too failed to foster agreement over the legality of the postponement and the legitimacy of the government following the expiration of its term. 


Having catalysed constitutional chaos, Mideksa set about facilitating Ahmed’s bypassing of various laws and bylaws to dissolve the Ethiopian People’s Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) and establish the Prosperity Party (PP). Beyond legal and procedural controversies, the move to reconstitute the EPRDF drew criticism for its intent. Abiy’s desire to dissolve the EPRDF and

“Medemer”

 (amalgamate) its constituent and affiliated parts was viewed by many as an initial step towards constitutional remaking and a reversal of multinational federalism.


The dissolution of the EPRDF ended the “reformist” coalition known as Team Lemma that propelled Abiy Ahmed to its chairmanship and Ethiopia’s prime ministership. In August 2020, Lemma Megersa, after whom Team Lemma was named, was removed from the Prosperity Party and as Minister of Defence for opposing the EPRDF’s amalgamation. The PP’s establishment was so ad hoc that it remains unclear if Megersa had actually joined the PP before he was booted out.


The relationship between the erstwhile allies came under strain as early as 2019 and was indicative of a wider rift between Abiy Ahmed and his Oromo base over the meaning of “reform” and its alignment with the demands of the protests that spurred Team Lemma’s rise. Ahmed positioned himself as an Oromo populist championing the cause of the Oromo farmer and, more broadly, seeking the “proper implementation of federalism”. Once in power, he started to appeal to a form of “pan-Ethiopian” nationalism which hoped to homogenize national identity and recentralize Ethiopia’s governing structures. Many in Ahmed’s Oromo base viewed the turn as a betrayal of the cause. Even before Megersa’s political downfall, suspicions over Ahmed’s intentions ignited a still-raging conflict with the Oromo Liberation Army. 


For a time, Abiy managed to force together the antagonistic nationalisms by offering a shared enemy – Tigrayan supremacy. Once considered the champion of the “national question”, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) was recast as the primary impediment to its “proper implementation”, while maintaining its long-held position as the primary impediment to the return of a unitary institutional setup. “Tigrinya speakers” became “daytime hyenas” on whom the country’s many political and social crises could be scapegoated. 


The TPLF opposed the postponement of the election and refused to recognize the federal government once its constitutionally set term was over. Unfortunately, the TPLF did not lodge an official challenge to the postponement through its seats in both chambers of parliament. Instead, it retreated into Tigray to shore up its base and made plans to hold a regional election within constitutionally set limits.


Both the dissolution of the EPRDF and the postponement of the elections drew widespread criticism from divergent opposition groups. Still, the TPLF’s concerns were dismissed as the mere disgruntlements of …

author: Huyam Salih and Obai Khalifa
title: Africa cannot build a stronger agrifood economy while the livestock sector loses $4 billion a year
content:
Across Africa, the livestock sector supports more than 350 million people. Livestock is much more than an agricultural commodity. For millions of families, cattle, sheep, goats, poultry, and other animals are sources of food and income. They are also productive assets that support trade, processing, services, employment and rural wealth creation. Despite its centrality to Africa’s wider agrifood economy, the systems that govern and influence the continent’s livestock sector remain among the most undercapitalised parts of African agriculture. Africa loses an estimated USD 4 billion every year due to unrealised livestock potential.


Too often, livestock farmers, particularly pastoralists and small-scale producers, are seen through the lens of subsistence and poverty. Investors see fragmented markets, climate exposure and informal production systems and conclude that the risks are too high. The challenge is therefore not only a shortage of capital, but an investability gap: fragmented supply, weak market information, uncertain offtake, and policy and regulatory uncertainty can make otherwise viable opportunities difficult to assess and finance.


Many countries also continue to face widespread circulation of substandard and falsified veterinary products, varying levels of regulatory capacity, high dependence on imported medicines and the escalating threat of antimicrobial resistance.


Public investment is central to addressing these challenges, but spending has often lagged behind government pledges. Under the 2003

Maputo Declaration on Agriculture and Food Security

, African governments pledged to allocate at least 10% of national budgets to agriculture and rural development. More than two decades later, most countries have fallen short. The persistent gap highlights the challenge governments face in financing the services and infrastructure needed to attract and sustain private investment.


Africa’s annual food import bill was estimated at around US

$70 billion

 in 2025, despite its wealth in arable land and livestock. Although this figure covers far more than livestock products, it underscores the scale of food demand that African producers could be better equipped to serve. Meeting more of that demand requires investment not only in production, but also in getting food reliably and competitively to market. The opportunity is not simply to import substitution; it is to build competitive African value chains capable of serving regional demand and other higher-value markets.


The

African Union–Inter-African Bureau for Animal Resources

 (AU-IBAR) is working to address these gaps by bringing together governments, regulators and investors to connect fragmented livestock markets. Its approach seeks to strengthen regional trade while improving farmers’ livelihoods and supporting rural economies.


Through the Integrated Regional Livestock Value Chain Transformation Programme (IRLVC), AU-IBAR links priority livestock value chains with regional trade corridors, market access and investment. The programme focuses on making cross-border trade more workable through coordinated standards and policies, while creating opportunities for private-sector participation and financing. Alongside this, the Africa Pastoral Markets Development (APMD) Platform strengthens pastoralists’ market participation and enterprise resilience and supports commercially viable investment pathways that could help unlock up to US$500 million in pastoral investment opportunities, while improving consumers’ access to livestock products.


Stronger regional markets could attract investment in processing, transport, feed and animal health services, supporting businesses and jobs across rural economies. Harmonised standards, more efficient trade corridors and coordinated disease control would lower barriers to trade and make markets more predictable for producers and investors. In economic terms, these are forms of market infrastructure: they lower transaction costs, reduce uncertainty and improve the risk-return proposition for investment. Ultimately, success should be measured not only in investment flows or trade volumes, but in better returns for farmers and more secure livelihoods for pastoral communities.


Across East Africa, countries are demonstrating what is possible with the right investment. Ethiopia, home to one of the world’s largest livestock populations, is

addressing gaps

 in feed, productivity, processing and markets through …

author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.


Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.


After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.


The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.


The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.


The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.


At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.


“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.


The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.


Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.
